newsitem.title: USA: MCI wins U.S. Postal contract, its largest deal ever.
newsitem.headline: MCI wins U.S. Postal contract, its largest deal ever.

text.p: MCI Communications Corp. won a contract worth up to $3 billion to manage the Postal Service's telecommunications network, the largest deal in the phone company's history, MCI announced Wednesday.
As part of the contract, MCI and its partners will create and manage a telecommunications network linking up to 34,000 post offices and other postal facilities, the company said.
The contract has a guaranteed value of at least $100 million and an upper limit of $3 billion if the Postal Service chooses to make full use of MCI services specified in the deal, the company said.
The initial contract covers five years and contains options for two three-year renewals, for a total of 11 years. It takes effect in 90 days, an MCI spokeswoman said.

Suppliers include San Jose, Calif.-based Cisco Systems Inc., the leading supplier of network equipment, and Digital Equipment Corp., a top computer systems company based in Maynard, Mass. The $3 billion ceiling on the deal covers only MCI services.

MCI, the nation's second largest long-distance carrier after AT&T Corp., is based in Washington. MCI Government Markets, its public-sector sales and marketing arm in McLean, Va., was the lead contractor on the deal.
MCI said that by running the Postal Service's network, it can help post office customer service by streamlining operations and creating ways of offering new kinds of services.

It said the project would improve the Postal Service's access to information contained on its widely dispersed computer systems and provide centralized software distribution and technical support for postal employees.
The project also will provide connections for a new retail computer system the Postal Service is installing throughout the quasi-government agency.
"The MCI network will give us the availability and responsiveness we need to meet our customers' expectations," said Rick Weirich, vice president of information services for the Postal Service.
MCI has agreed to a $20 billion merger with British Telecommunications Plc. The deal, which awaits shareholder votes and a series of regulatory approvals, is not expected to close until this fall.

MCI's largest prior contract was a $1.4 billion deal awarded in 1994 to build and manage a telecommunications network for a U.S. insurance consortium, including New York Life Insurance Co. and Nationwide Mutual Insurance Co., an MCI spokeswoman said.

MCI stock dipped 12.5 cents to $38.125 in afternoon trading on Nasdaq. Cisco stock rose $4 to $51.875, also on Nasdaq, and Digital Equipment edged up 25 cents to $29 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
